title: Power of a machine: Distinguishing power from work
question: What is the efficiency of the machine?
diagramSvg: <svg class="q-diagram-svg" viewBox="0 0 320 145" width="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M30 20 H290" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="5" /><path d="M160 24 V67" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="2.5" /><rect x="124" y="67" width="72" height="37" rx="3" fill="#94a3b8" stroke="#475569" /><text x="160" y="89" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#111827">400 N</text><path d="M217 100 V65" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M211 77 L217 65 L223 77" fill="none" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="228" y="77" font-size="10" fill="#16a34a">2.5 m</text><text x="160" y="126" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">Time = 5 s</text></svg>
explanation:
Useful work:


W_{out}=400(2.5)=1000,J


Useful output power:


P_{out}=(1000 / 5)=200,W


Therefore,


eta=(200 / 250)×100=80%


Option D incorrectly assumes that all input power becomes useful output power.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank

title: Inclined plane: Calculating efficiency from forces and geometry
question: What is the efficiency of the plane?

explanation:
VR=(6 / 2)=3



MA=(360 / 180)=2


Therefore,


eta=frac23×100=66.7%


The correct answer is **C**, not A. Option A would result from using an incorrect velocity ratio.

title: First-class lever: Unequal arms and mechanical advantage
question: What is the effort required to keep the lever in equilibrium, and what is its ideal mechanical advantage?
diagramSvg: <svg class="q-diagram-svg" viewBox="0 0 340 145" width="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M28 62 H310" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" /><path d="M130 65 L112 97 L148 97 Z" fill="#94a3b8" stroke="#475569" stroke-width="1.5" /><path d="M61 14 V55" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M55 46 L61 57 L67 46" fill="none" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M268 14 V55" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M262 46 L268 57 L274 46" fill="none" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="61" y="11" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#dc2626">300 N</text><text x="268" y="11" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#2563eb">E</text><text x="130" y="111" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">F</text><path d="M61 120 H130 M130 120 H268" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="3 3" /><text x="95" y="135" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">20 cm</text><text x="199" y="135" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">60 cm</text></svg>
explanation:
Taking moments about the fulcrum:


300×20=E×60



E=(300×20 / 60)=100,N


The ideal mechanical advantage is


MA=(Load / Effort)
=(300 / 100)=3


Option B reverses the load-to-effort ratio. Option C incorrectly multiplies the load by the ratio of the effort arm to the load arm.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank

title: Third-class lever: Distinguishing MA from VR
question: If the lever is in equilibrium, which pair correctly gives the effort and the ideal velocity ratio?
diagramSvg: <svg class="q-diagram-svg" viewBox="0 0 340 145" width="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M38 80 H307" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" /><path d="M38 83 L22 111 H54 Z" fill="#94a3b8" stroke="#475569" /><path d="M78 29 V72" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M72 40 L78 28 L84 40" fill="none" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="78" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#2563eb">E</text><path d="M278 29 V72" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M272 62 L278 74 L284 62" fill="none" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="278" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#dc2626">60 N</text><text x="38" y="125" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">F</text><path d="M38 117 H78 M78 117 H278" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="3 3" /><text x="58" y="139" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="currentColor">5 cm</text><text x="178" y="139" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">30 cm from F</text></svg>
explanation:
Taking moments about the elbow:


E×5=60×30



E=(1800 / 5)=360,N


The ideal VR is the effort-arm to load-arm ratio:


VR=(5 / 30)=frac16


This means the correct physical pair is E=360,N and VR=frac16, which is **option B**.

Option D incorrectly uses the reciprocal of VR. A third-class lever can require an effort greater than its load while providing a distance or speed advantage.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank

title: Inclined plane: Finding the height from efficiency
question: A machine in the form of an inclined plane has a length of 8,m, a mechanical advantage of 3, and an efficiency of 75%. What is the vertical height of the plane?
explanation:
eta=(MA / VR)×100



75=(3 / VR)×100



VR=4


For an inclined plane,


VR=(l / h)


Thus,


h=(8 / 4)=2,m


Option D results from incorrectly using the mechanical advantage as the velocity ratio.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank

title: Block and tackle: Actual effort and velocity ratio
question: An ideal block-and-tackle system has five rope segments supporting its movable block. It raises a 750,N load at constant speed. What effort is required, and how far must the effort move to raise the load by 24,cm?
explanation:
For an ideal block and tackle with five supporting strands,


VR=5,qquad MA=5


Effort:


E=(750 / 5)=150,N


Effort displacement:


d_E=VR× d_L=5×24=120,cm


Option C calculates the effort correctly but uses an incorrect displacement.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank

title: Experimental graph: Effort displacement versus load displacement
question: What is the machine’s velocity ratio according to this experiment?
diagramSvg: <svg viewBox="0 0 460 190" width="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="background:#f8fafc; border-radius:8px; border:1px solid #cbd5e1; font-family:system-ui, sans-serif;"><text x="230" y="24" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">HOTS Analytical Diagram: Experimental graph: Effort displacement versus load displacement</text><rect x="40" y="45" width="380" height="95" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#cbd5e1"/><text x="230" y="72" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="700" fill="#1e40af">High Order Thinking Principles</text><text x="230" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="#334155">Refer to the experimental variables and quantitative relationships in the problem</text><text x="230" y="114" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9.5" font-weight="600" fill="#16a34a">Rigorous ICSE Class 10 Syllabus Correlation</text><text x="230" y="165" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" font-weight="600" fill="#64748b">Standard Analytical Schema</text></svg>
explanation:
The gradient of the graph is


(d_E / d_L)=(40 / 10)=4


By definition, VR=d_E/d_L, so the answer is 4.

Option A takes the reciprocal. Option D confuses the effort displacement with the ratio.

**Correction to Q6:** The correct answer is **B**, not D. The effort is 360,N, and VR=5/30=1/6. The earlier answer label was incorrect.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank

title: First-class lever with the bar’s weight acting on the opposite side
question: What effort is required for equilibrium?
diagramSvg: <svg class="q-diagram-svg" viewBox="0 0 340 155" width="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M25 65 H315" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" /><path d="M122 68 L105 96 H139 Z" fill="#94a3b8" stroke="#475569" /><path d="M25 15 V57" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M19 46 L25 58 L31 46" fill="none" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="25" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="#dc2626">180 N</text><path d="M170 15 V57" stroke="#7c3aed" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M164 46 L170 58 L176 46" fill="none" stroke="#7c3aed" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="170" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="#7c3aed">60 N</text><path d="M315 112 V70" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M309 82 L315 70 L321 82" fill="none" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="315" y="126" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#2563eb">E</text><text x="122" y="112" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">F</text><path d="M25 136 H122 M122 136 H315" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="3 3" /><text x="73" y="149" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">0.4 m</text><text x="218" y="149" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">0.8 m</text></svg>
explanation:
The load produces an anticlockwise moment about F:


180(0.4)=72,N,m


The bar's centre is 0.2,m to the right of F, so its weight produces a clockwise moment of


60(0.2)=12,N,m


The effort arm is 0.8,m. Therefore,


72=12+0.8E



E=(60 / 0.8)=75,N


The correct effort is 75,N, which is absent from the choices. This question is invalid as originally offered; the correct answer must not be forced to match an incorrect option.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank

title: Movable pulley with an additional downward force
question: What is the effort required to raise the system at constant speed?
diagramSvg: <svg class="q-diagram-svg" viewBox="0 0 340 195" width="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M35 20 H305" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="5" /><path d="M75 23 V91 A45 45 0 0 0 165 91 V43" fill="none" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="2.5" /><circle cx="120" cy="91" r="25" fill="none" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="3" /><path d="M120 116 V127" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="3" /><rect x="82" y="127" width="76" height="30" rx="3" fill="#94a3b8" stroke="#475569" /><text x="120" y="146" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#111827">250 N</text><path d="M120 157 V180" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M114 169 L120 181 L126 169" fill="none" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="132" y="178" font-size="10" fill="#dc2626">50 N</text><path d="M165 79 V40" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M159 51 L165 39 L171 51" fill="none" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="181" y="48" font-size="11" fill="#2563eb">E</text></svg>
explanation:
The total downward force is


250+50=300,N


Two rope segments support the assembly, so


2E=300Rightarrow E=150,N


The correct answer is **B**, not C. Option C would result from an incorrect total-force calculation.

title: Inclined plane: Finding friction from the measured effort
question: What is the frictional force opposing the motion?
diagramSvg: <svg class="q-diagram-svg" viewBox="0 0 320 150" width="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M25 125 H285 L285 48 Z" fill="#cbd5e1" fill-opacity="0.5" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="2" /><path d="M25 125 L285 48" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="3" /><rect x="134" y="80" width="36" height="23" rx="2" transform="rotate(-16.5 152 91)" fill="#94a3b8" stroke="#475569" /><path d="M164 78 L207 65" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M195 59 L209 64 L199 73" fill="none" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="211" y="60" font-size="10" fill="#16a34a">220 N</text><text x="130" y="143" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">5 m</text><text x="291" y="91" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">3 m</text></svg>
explanation:
The component of the load’s weight parallel to the plane is


300(3 / 5)=180,N


At constant speed, the effort balances this component plus friction:


220=180+f



f=40,N


The correct answer is **A**, not B. Option B results from an incorrect subtraction.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank

title: Lever: Finding the centre of gravity from a balancing diagram
question: What upward effort balances the bar?
diagramSvg: <svg class="q-diagram-svg" viewBox="0 0 320 140" width="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M20 60 H300" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="5" /><path d="M160 63 L143 91 H177 Z" fill="#94a3b8" stroke="#475569" /><path d="M112 13 V52" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M106 41 L112 53 L118 41" fill="none" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="112" y="11" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="#dc2626">120 N</text><path d="M300 101 V64" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M294 76 L300 64 L306 76" fill="none" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="300" y="116" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="#2563eb">E</text><path d="M160 14 V52" stroke="#7c3aed" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M154 41 L160 53 L166 41" fill="none" stroke="#7c3aed" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="160" y="11" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="#7c3aed">90 N</text><text x="160" y="107" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">F</text><text x="136" y="135" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">0.3 m</text><text x="235" y="135" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">0.9 m</text></svg>
explanation:
The bar’s own weight acts at F, so it produces zero moment about F.


120(0.3)=E(0.9)



E=(36 / 0.9)=40,N


Option C incorrectly assigns a moment to the bar’s weight even though it acts through the pivot.

title: Lever with an inclined effort: Only the perpendicular component produces a moment
question: What effort balances the lever?
diagramSvg: <svg class="q-diagram-svg" viewBox="0 0 340 170" width="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M24 85 H312" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" /><path d="M132 88 L116 117 H148 Z" fill="#94a3b8" stroke="#475569" /><path d="M66 22 V76" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M60 65 L66 77 L72 65" fill="none" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="66" y="16" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#dc2626">100 N</text><path d="M274 85 L250 26" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M249 40 L249 25 L262 32" fill="none" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="277" y="24" font-size="11" fill="#2563eb">E</text><path d="M274 43 V85" stroke="#94a3b8" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="3 3" /><path d="M274 57 A28 28 0 0 0 263 59" fill="none" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="1.5" /><text x="281" y="62" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">30°</text><text x="132" y="131" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">F</text><text x="70" y="151" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">20 cm</text><text x="214" y="151" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">50 cm</text></svg>
explanation:
Only the component perpendicular to the lever contributes to the turning moment. Since the force makes 30^° with the vertical, its vertical component is Ecos30^°.


100(0.20)=Ecos30^°(0.50)



E=(20 / 0.50cos30^°)
≈46.2,N


Option A ignores the angle; option C incorrectly treats the perpendicular component as Esin30^°.

**Correction to Q9 — replacement question:** The effort must act **downward**, not upward, at B. With the 200,N load at A, the 100,N bar weight, and the same distances, the required downward effort is 33.3,N. This follows from 200(0.5)=100(0.5)+E(1.5).

**Correction to Q11:** The correct answer is **B (40,N**, as shown by the two successive force divisions. The answer label C was a mistake.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank

title: Block and tackle: Inferring the load from effort displacement
question: An ideal block-and-tackle system has a velocity ratio of 6. The effort moves through 1.8,m, and the load rises through 0.3,m. If the applied effort is 150,N, what load is raised?
explanation:
The displacement ratio confirms


VR=(1.8 / 0.3)=6


For an ideal machine, MA=VR=6. Thus,


L=MA× E=6(150)=900,N


Option B incorrectly uses a ratio of 5.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank

    <text x="140" y="106" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">F</text>
    <text x="91" y="135" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">40 cm</text>
    <text x="229" y="135" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">80 cm</text>
  </svg>
explanation:
MA=(450 / 150)=3



VR=(80 / 40)=2


Thus,


eta=(3 / 2)×100=150%


This exceeds 100%, which is physically impossible for a passive machine under the stated conditions. The observations are inconsistent: the measured forces, lever arms and claimed steady operation cannot all be correct. This question is withdrawn rather than assigning a physically impossible efficiency.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank

title: The Load on a Wheelbarrow
question: A load of 200 N is carried in a wheelbarrow at a distance of 0.4 m from the wheel axle (fulcrum). If the effort is applied vertically upwards at a distance of 1.2 m from the axle, what is the minimum effort required to lift the load?
diagramSvg: <svg class="q-diagram-svg" viewBox="0 0 340 150" width="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><circle cx="42" cy="111" r="16" fill="none" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="3" /><circle cx="42" cy="111" r="3" fill="#64748b" /><path d="M42 111 L266 51" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" /><path d="M266 51 L309 39" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" /><path d="M101 95 L140 55 L176 87 Z" fill="#cbd5e1" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="2" /><path d="M140 55 L140 24" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M134 35 L140 23 L146 35" fill="none" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="140" y="18" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#dc2626">L</text><path d="M289 35 V8" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M283 19 L289 7 L295 19" fill="none" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="306" y="12" font-size="11" fill="#2563eb">E</text><text x="42" y="139" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">F</text><path d="M42 132 H140 M140 132 H289" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="3 3" /><text x="91" y="145" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">40 cm</text><text x="214" y="145" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">120 cm from F</text></svg>
explanation: By the principle of moments for a Class II lever: Effort × Effort Arm = Load × Load Arm. Effort × 1.2 m = 200 N × 0.4 m => Effort × 1.2 = 80 => Effort = 80 / 1.2 = 66.7 N.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank

title: Uniform lever: Accounting for the weight of the bar
question: What upward effort is needed to balance the bar?
diagramSvg: <svg class="q-diagram-svg" viewBox="0 0 340 160" width="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M24 70 H316" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" /><path d="M96 73 L79 101 H113 Z" fill="#94a3b8" stroke="#475569" stroke-width="1.5" /><path d="M24 17 V61" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M18 50 L24 62 L30 50" fill="none" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="24" y="12" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="#dc2626">200 N</text><path d="M316 114 V79" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M310 90 L316 78 L322 90" fill="none" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="316" y="128" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2563eb">E</text><path d="M170 22 V60" stroke="#7c3aed" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M164 49 L170 61 L176 49" fill="none" stroke="#7c3aed" stroke-width="2.5" /><text x="170" y="16" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="#7c3aed">100 N</text><text x="96" y="115" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">F</text><text x="24" y="145" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">A</text><text x="316" y="145" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">B</text><text x="58" y="137" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">0.5 m</text><text x="205" y="137" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">1.5 m</text></svg>
explanation:
Take moments about F. The load at A produces an anticlockwise moment:


200×0.5=100,N,m


The bar’s weight acts at its centre, 1.0,m from A, which is 0.5,m to the right of F. It produces a clockwise moment of 100×0.5=50,N,m.

The effort acts 1.5,m from F and produces an anticlockwise moment:


E(1.5)+100=50


Thus,


E=-33.3,N


The negative result means the assumed upward effort cannot balance this configuration; the effort must act downward. Therefore, the question as drawn has no valid listed answer. **This item is withdrawn and will be replaced by a physically consistent question.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank

title: First-class lever: Calculating the fulcrum position
question: A weightless lever is 1.5,m long. A load of 240,N acts at the left end, and an upward effort of 80,N acts at the right end. The lever balances horizontally. How far is the fulcrum from the left end?
explanation:
Let the fulcrum be x metres from the left end. Its distance from the right end is 1.5-x.

By the principle of moments,


240x=80(1.5-x)



240x=120-80x



320x=120



x=0.375,m


Option C incorrectly assumes equal lever arms.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank

title: Two students make the following statements about an ordinary real machine:
question: - Student P: “Its efficiency can be 100% if the effort is applied very slowly.” - Student Q: “Its efficiency may be improved by reducing friction, even if its velocity ratio remains unchanged.” Which statement is correct?

options.text: Both P and Q are correct.
P is correct, but Q is incorrect.
P is incorrect, but Q is correct.
Both P and Q are incorrect.

explanation: Applying effort slowly does not eliminate friction or other energy losses, so it does not guarantee 100% efficiency. Reducing friction can increase efficiency while the velocity ratio remains unchanged.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank

title: Combined numerical problem: MA, VR and efficiency
question: A machine raises a load of 720,N using an effort of 180,N. During the operation, the effort moves 2.4,m while the load moves 0.6,m. Calculate its efficiency and the energy wasted if the effort completes this displacement once.
explanation:
Mechanical advantage:


MA=(720 / 180)=4


Velocity ratio:


VR=(2.4 / 0.6)=4


Therefore,


eta=frac44×100=100%


Input work:


W_{in}=180(2.4)=432,J


Useful output work:


W_{out}=720(0.6)=432,J


Thus, the energy wasted is 0,J. The correct answer is **D**, not B.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank

title: Inclined plane: Frictional work and efficiency
question: A 400,N load is pulled up a rough inclined plane of length 5,m and height 3,m. The effort parallel to the plane is 300,N. Calculate the work done against friction.
explanation:
Input work:


W_{in}=300×5=1500,J


Useful work against gravity:


W_{useful}=400×3=1200,J


Work dissipated against friction:


W_f=1500-1200=300,J


The correct answer is **A**, not C.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank

title: Movable pulley: Acceleration is not constant speed
question: A 180,N load is attached to an ideal movable pulley. The upward effort is 120,N. What is the net force on the movable assembly, including the load, and in which direction does it act? Ignore the pulley’s mass.
explanation:
Two rope segments each have tension 120,N, so the total upward force is


2T=240,N


The downward load is 180,N, giving a net force of


240-180=60,N


The net force is actually **60,N upward**, so the correct answer is **A**, not B. A downward net force would occur only if the total downward force exceeded the upward support.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank

title: Comparing two machines by efficiency
question: Machine P raises a 400,N load through 2,m using 1,200,J of input work. Machine Q raises a 500,N load through 1.5,m using 1,000,J of input work. Which statement is correct?

options.text: P is more efficient by 5 percentage points.
Q is more efficient by 5 percentage points.
P is more efficient by 10 percentage points.

explanation:
For P:


eta_P=(400(2) / 1200)×100
=66.7%


For Q:


eta_Q=(500(1.5) / 1000)×100
=75%


Thus Q is more efficient by approximately 8.3 percentage points. The correct answer is not among the options; this item is withdrawn rather than assigning a false comparison.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank
